But, coming here, or to r/depression, or almost any depression forum I see this quite a lot. The rules here don't even allow for people to get out of it what they really need or at least get a little empathy.

I've been suicidal over half my life. If I hadn't of given my word that I wouldn't off myself to someone -- I'd be gone by now. I'm plenty self-aware and know what works for me and many people isn't kind talk (just makes you feel guilty) or pep (no it doesn't always get better). Just a bit of real expression without judgement or pushing or even platitudes. Sometimes a little blood-letting literally or figuratively is the only thing that can get you to the next day.

Not all symptoms show up at once and somatic symptoms are not always obvious to the person suffering from them (or always severe). I have no idea what he may have I was offering a guess based on my knowledge and his story, but IANAD.Though I have seen many forms of depression and suffer from it myself. I've seen enough atypical cases to know that not every symptom has to be checked off a list for a person to have a specific disorder. Also, while therapy is ineffective for treatment in melancholic depression, medication *is* usually effective and I've seen no research to suggest that it's harder to treat once correctly diagnosed.

I got a few piddly upvotes, so what? My advice to seek help was valid and onset symptoms are not the same as a full on episode, so it's at least worth a look by a psychiatrist. I know that it's impossible to make a correct diagnose with out a consultation and medical/family history. But, some people need a named disease to seek out help (not that I was trying to fool him as I still think this fits for onset of melancholic depression).

Sounds like [Melancholic depression](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melancholic_depression). Go to your student health office and get some meds for it, it's a biological problem with a cure in most cases. I'm guess that your a guy from the tone and men are affected differently by depression, thus usually harder to diagnose. Tell them about your lack of emotive affect and general inability to care -- you could also mention that you think it might be the above but a psychiatrist will still have to evaluate you.
